newsitem.title: UK: Russia and China Eurobonds meet with wide approval.
newsitem.headline: Russia and China Eurobonds meet with wide approval.

text.p: Sovereign issuance was to the fore in the Eurobond market on Thursday as Russia and China launched successful transactions and Cyprus made its market debut.
Heavy demand for Russian paper after a series of roadshows around the world which ended on Wednesday allowed it to ask for $2.0 billion over 10 years, twice the size originally touted.
While final pricing was not due until later a spread of 375 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, dealers said the issue was already trading four or five b.p. tighter.
Last Friday, Russian deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov told a news conference it would borrow up to $3.5 billion from international bond markets this year.
That figure was based on Russia also launching a global dollar bond in the autumn.
Today's deal was launched with a 10.00 percent coupon by joint lead managers J.P. Morgan Securities and SBC Warburg.
Double-digit coupons are something of a rarity in the current low interest rate environment and are particularly attractive to retail investors.

"It's obviously caught the eye of the institutional investor. It was very well received in Asia and then in Europe. We would expect the same in New York," said one trader closely involved in the Russian deal.
Another trader said: "It will be many times oversubscribed. There is demand for longer duration in the emerging sector."
The deal, modern Russia's third since its market debut last November, ranks among the largest Eurobonds ever.
"It has given them the flexibility to be more opportunistic if they want to do another deal later this year, partly as pre-funding for 1998," a syndicate manager said.
Elsewhere, China's first Eurobond this year, a 500 million mark five-year at a 55 b.p. spread, was heavily oversubscribed, new issues managers said.
"We were three to four times oversubscribed," an official at joint lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. "We have no bonds left, and people are really trying to get hold of them."
China last tapped the international bond markets in July 1996, when it issued dollar transactions. It has no outstanding mark Eurobonds.
"China created a kind of collector's item by keeping the size of the deal so small," the Deutsche official said.
"It is the only bond available from the People's Republic in marks, so for many investors it is the only way to get this kind of diversification."

Deutsche said the bonds were bought by a broad mix of investors. Around a quarter went to retail investors, and mutual fund managers, central banks and bank asset allocation departments were also buyers.
About a third of the deal was sold in Germany, with slightly less going to Asia accounts and into Britain, Deutsche said.
China is very much an international focus, with the handover of Hong Kong by Britain now only 12 days away.
Cyprus made its debut in the Eurobond market with a $300 million five-year transaction via SBC Warburg said.
The size was at the upper end of the $200-$300 million range being touted earlier in the week.
The deal was reoffered at a 37 b.p. spread, and tightened gently to a 37 36 b.p. quote on borker screens.
The bond was issued under a $500 million Euro medium-term note (EMTN) programme recently established by Cyprus.
The proceeds will be used to refinance existing debt and to fund development project.
-- Dan Lalor, London newsroom +44 171 542 8863
